title: The projection formula with a finitely presented constant coefficient
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and assume $R^qf_*F=0$ for every sheaf of $A$-modules $F$ and every $q>N$, for one integer $N\geq0$. Work in the unbounded derived categories of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaves on the small étale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $K\in D^-(X_{\Et},A)$, where $D^-$ means that the cohomology sheaves vanish in all sufficiently large degrees. Let $M$ be a finitely presented $A$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], with $M_X,M_Y$ the associated constant sheaves [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. Then the canonical projection map
$$
Rf_*K\otimes^L_AM_Y\longrightarrow Rf_*\bigl(K\otimes^L_AM_X\bigr)
$$
is an isomorphism. Here derived tensor is the ordinary uncompleted étale derived tensor of [def-kun-derived-tensor], and $Rf_*$ and the canonical projection morphism are the unbounded K-injective direct image and its adjunction mate of [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. The map is natural in $M$.

proof.text: For a bounded-above complex $Q$ of $A$-modules, write $Q_T$ for its termwise constant complex on $T_{\Et}$. The constant functor is exact: the constant presheaf functor is sectionwise exact, and sheafification is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact]. The canonical inverse-image isomorphism for constant sets of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-constant-sheaf] respects addition and scalar multiplication, since both sides send every constant element to the same constant element; it therefore identifies $f^{-1}Q_Y$ with $Q_X$, naturally and termwise. The inverse image on modules is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Define $\alpha_Q=\mathrm{PF}_f(K,Q_Y)$ using [def-kun-projection-formula-map], followed by this identification. Explicitly its adjunct is $f^{-1}(Rf_*K\otimes_A^L Q_Y)\cong f^{-1}Rf_*K\otimes_A^L Q_X\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_K\otimes1}K\otimes_A^L Q_X$. This construction is natural in $Q$; its value for $Q=M[0]$ is the map in the statement.

By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], the two functors of the coefficient sheaf are exact, the projection transformation gives a morphism of distinguished triangles including the connecting square, and its value at $A_Y$ is the identity of $Rf_*K$ under the unit identifications. Exactness of the constant functor from Step 1 carries shifts and cone triangles of module complexes to the corresponding sheaf triangles. For $Q=A^s$ the map is the direct sum of $s$ unit maps, because additive functors preserve finite biproducts and naturality determines its restrictions to their summands. Thus $\alpha_Q$ is an isomorphism for finite free modules and their shifts. A bounded finite free complex has a finite filtration by brutal truncations whose successive quotients are its shifted individual terms. Applying the morphism of triangles and the long exact cohomology sequences [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] on each five-term segment shows by induction that $\alpha_Q$ is an isomorphism on every cohomology sheaf. The criterion [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] then makes $\alpha_Q$ an isomorphism for every bounded finite free complex.

proof.text: The finite presentation gives a finite free surjection $P^0\twoheadrightarrow M$. Its kernel is finitely generated by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]; choose a finite free module surjecting onto that kernel. Repeat on the kernel of this new surjection. This constructs an exact augmented resolution $P\to M$ with finite free terms in nonpositive degrees. For $m\geq0$ put $P_m=\sigma_{\geq-m}P$ and $C_m=\operatorname{Cone}(P_m\to M)$. Explicitly $C_m^0=M$, $C_m^i=P_m^{i+1}$ for $i<0$, and $C_m^i=0$ for $i>0$; its differential into degree zero is the augmentation, and its lower differentials are the negatives of those of $P$. Surjectivity of $P^0\to M$ makes $H^0(C_m)=0$, including when $m=0$. For $m\geq1$, exactness of the augmented resolution makes $H^i(C_m)=0$ for $-m\leq i\leq-1$, while $H^{-m-1}(C_m)=\ker(d_P^{-m})$. For $m=0$ the only possible cohomology is $H^{-1}(C_0)=\ker(P^0\to M)$. Thus in every case $C_m\in D^{\leq-m-1}(A)$. These assertions also follow directly from the cone differential, without asserting that the resolution terminates.

proof.text: The module direct image is additive and left exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact], and its source abelian category has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Apply [lem-sf-finite-cd-derived-upper-bound] to $F=f_*$ and the assumed bound $N$. Its total derived functor is the $Rf_*$ used in Step 1, by uniqueness of the total right derived functor. Thus $Rf_*$ carries $D^{\leq t}(X_{\Et},A)$ into $D^{\leq t+N}(Y_{\Et},A)$ for every integer $t$. In particular choose $b$ with $K\in D^{\leq b}$; then $Rf_*K\in D^{\leq b+N}$. This uses the unbounded upper-bound theorem, not a convergence assertion for a bounded-below spectral sequence applied outside its domain.

source.place: Tag 07K7, lemma-unbounded-right-derived, (4)(c), with n=N+1 and lower endpoint -infinity.

proof.text: On either small étale site the following tensor estimate is elementary from [lem-kun-bounded-flat-replacement] and [lem-kun-kflat-criteria]: if $E\in D^{\leq a}$ and $G\in D^{\leq c}$, first replace representing complexes by their smart upper truncations at $a,c$, and then by the flat representatives with the same upper term bounds. They are K-flat, so their total tensor computes $E\otimes_A^LG$; a degree $n>a+c$ has no summand with $p\leq a$, $q\leq c$, $p+q=n$. Hence $E\otimes_A^LG\in D^{\leq a+c}$. Exactness of constant sheaves (Step 1) gives $(C_m)_T\in D^{\leq-m-1}$. Together with Step 4 and [lem-sf-finite-cd-derived-upper-bound], this gives both $Rf_*K\otimes_A^L(C_m)_Y$ and $Rf_*(K\otimes_A^L(C_m)_X)$ in $D^{\leq b+N-m-1}$: for the second expression tensor first, obtaining the bound $b-m-1$, and then apply $Rf_*$.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; bounded-above flat replacement is the existing lem-kun-bounded-flat-replacement (cycle-pullback construction, derived.tex Tag 05T7). The upper bound for direct image is derived.tex Tag 07K7 (4)(c).

proof.text: Apply the two exact coefficient functors and the projection transformation of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] to the triangle $(P_m)_Y\to M_Y\to(C_m)_Y\to$. For a fixed integer $r$, choose $m\geq0$ such that $b+N-m-1<r-1$. Step 5 makes the cohomology in degrees $r-1$ and $r$ of both resulting third terms zero. Their long exact sequences [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] therefore show that both horizontal maps from the expressions with $P_m$ to the expressions with $M$ are isomorphisms on $\mathcal H^r$. Naturality of $\alpha$ gives a commutative square with these maps as horizontal sides, $\mathcal H^r(\alpha_{P_m})$ as its left side and $\mathcal H^r(\alpha_M)$ as its right side. The left side is an isomorphism by Step 2. Solving the square for the right side makes it an isomorphism. This holds for every $r$, so [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] proves $\alpha_M$ is an isomorphism. The construction in Step 1 already proves naturality in $M$; no natural choice of free resolution is needed.

lean.statement: theorem isIso_finiteConstantProjectionMap (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (N : ℕ) (hcd : ∀ (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) (q : ℕ), N < q → IsZero ((_root_.DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ (q : ℤ)).obj ((lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f).rightDerivedFunctor.obj ((_root_.DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj F)))) (K : DerivedCategoryModule A X) (hK : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ q : ℤ, b < q → IsZero ((_root_.DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj K)) (M : ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) [Module.FinitePresentation A M] : IsIso ((finiteConstantProjectionMap A f K).app M)
lean.note: The helper is the canonical projection natural transformation restricted to constant modules and transported by the canonical single-degree inverse-image and constant-sheaf isomorphisms. Its NatTrans type includes naturality in M. No replacement of the canonical map, ring, site or unbounded derived category.
